blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Biodiversity is the cumulative product of over 3.5 billion years of evolutionary processes and ecological interactions.
Genetic variations arising from mutations and recombination serve as the foundational raw material for evolution.
Natural selection acts on phenotypic variations, enhancing the reproductive fitness of adapted individuals.
Adaptive radiation enables a common ancestral lineage to diversify into distinct ecological niches.

blocks.content: Biodiversity is the cumulative result of evolutionary changes shaped by natural selection over billions of years.

rows: Does not share a recent common ancestor
Forelimbs of whales, bats, and humans

items: Homologous organs signify divergent evolution and common ancestral origin (e.g., forelimbs of humans and bats).
Analogous organs demonstrate convergent evolution in response to similar environmental pressures (e.g., wings of birds and insects).
Darwin's Finches are the most frequently cited example of adaptive radiation and geographic speciation in competitive exams.
